text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Yemeni government says controversial Islamic preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala is not a Yemeni citizen, contrary to allegations by Kenyan authorities.
- Confusion and claims of irregularities continue to mar on-going voter registration, while opposition leaders make fresh appeals for an extension of the exercise.
- The Kenyan government seeks Parliament's approval to guarantee a 4.6 billion shillings ($85 million) loan from the Japanese government to the Kenya Posts & Telecommunications Corporation.
- Opposition party, FORD-Kenya says the government must agree to constitutional reforms amid calls for a national referendum for Kenyans to decide whether they want reforms or not.
- The government denies allegations saying it has used the Nyayo car project as a conduit to siphon public money into individuals pockets.
- The Electoral Commission temporarily suspends voter registration in Siaya District, Western Kenya.
- Four directors and three managers of Mbo-i-Kamiti Farmers Company are charged with stealing 10 million shillings from the company.
- President Daniel arap Moi asks Nairobi City Council to consider closing one section of a Nairobi street once a week to enable hawkers to sell their wares. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
